author: Johanna M. Menzel
title: The Sinophilism of J. H. G. Justi
role_description: China/Chinese civilization functions as an intellectual model and represented source within an eighteenth-century German European genealogy
interpretive_note: Useful anti-linearity control: China remains a source/object inside European intellectual history even as internally addressed Asian cases begin to appear elsewhere.

author: Arnold H. Rowbotham
title: The Jesuit Figurists and Eighteenth-Century Religious Thought
role_description: Chinese classical materials move through Jesuit figurist interpretation into eighteenth-century European religious/intellectual controversy
interpretive_note: A dense mediation case: Chinese texts matter through missionary translation, interpretation and circulation rather than as a self-contained Chinese intellectual history.

author: Ursula Lamb
title: Religious Conflicts in the Conquest of Mexico
role_description: Rival religious world-views under armed intercultural contact are treated as a history-of-ideas problem of conflict, acculturation and attempted substitution
interpretive_note: Especially important because Lamb explicitly argues that compulsory contacts between civilizations and acculturation should become objects of historical history-of-ideas analysis, not remain only anthropology/political history.

author: George Sansom
title: Early Sources of Japanese Tradition
role_description: Review treatment of primary/source architecture for Japanese tradition inside JHI
interpretive_note: Review presence matters for field infrastructure: Japan enters not only as source for Europe but as a tradition with its own source corpus requiring historiographical evaluation.

author: Max Hamburger
title: Aristotle and Confucius: A Comparison
role_description: Confucius and Aristotle are placed as explicit co-cases in comparative philosophy
interpretive_note: A useful pre-1960 International Society comparator: parity at the title/problem level already exists before Loehr/Hightower, though the precise comparative asymmetries require article-level reading.

author: Arthur F. Wright
title: The Study of Chinese Civilization
role_description: How Chinese civilization should be studied historically; disciplinary reconstruction of Sinology toward history/social science
interpretive_note: Major field-method marker; later 1964 peer explicitly reads it as freeing Sinology from the 'incubus of Orientalism' by learning to write history and use social science.

author: Max Loehr
title: The Question of Individualism in Chinese Art
role_description: Chinese art used as a core co-case for the International Society's individualism problem
interpretive_note: Not supplementary tail material: opens the issue generated from the Cambridge International Society meeting.

author: James R. Hightower
title: Individualism in Chinese Literature
role_description: Chinese literature as a core comparative site for individualism
interpretive_note: Pairs with Loehr; strong sign that Chinese materials have moved into the central conference/problem architecture.

author: Nicholas Rescher
title: Al-Fārābī on Logical Tradition
role_description: Al-Fārābī's logical work and place in Arabic-speaking philosophical tradition are treated as the article's principal intellectual-historical object
interpretive_note: Important pre-Fakhry internal-object marker: Islamic philosophy is not functioning chiefly as an intermediary to Europe; Rescher opens by stressing al-Fārābī's stature within Islam and Arabic logical studies.

author: Franco Venturi
title: Oriental Despotism
role_description: Genealogy and critique of the European concept of Oriental despotism
interpretive_note: Necessary negative/control role: wider regional coverage can coexist with continued study of 'the Orient' as a European conceptual construction rather than internally addressed Asian thought.

author: Arturo Ardao
title: Assimilation and Transformation of Positivism in Latin America
role_description: Latin-American actors and traditions selectively assimilate and transform an imported positivist programme
interpretive_note: Strongly extends the 1949 Mexican revolt case: reception is neither passive diffusion nor derivative repetition but regional intellectual transformation, well before the 1975 Zea review.

author: Majid Fakhry
title: Al-Farabi and the Reconciliation of Plato and Aristotle
role_description: Al-Farabi treated as an actor reconstructing/reconciling philosophical authorities within Islamic philosophy
interpretive_note: Important shift beyond Arabic philosopher merely as intermediary to Europe; actor's own conceptual operation is the article's object.

author: Conrad Schirokauer
title: Balazs on China
role_description: Review of China-focused scholarship inside JHI
interpretive_note: Evidence that Chinese civilizational/history scholarship has a review-discussion presence as a field, not only isolated source cases.

author: Ainslie T. Embree
title: Ways of Thinking of Eastern Peoples: India-China-Tibet-Japan
role_description: JHI review of Hajime Nakamura's comparative Asian thought project spanning multiple internally differentiated Asian traditions
interpretive_note: Critical network marker: Nakamura's anti-monolithic comparative thought project enters JHI through review immediately after the Wiener/Nakamura transpacific collaboration reconstructed elsewhere in the repo.

author: Dale Riepe
title: Emerson and Indian Philosophy
role_description: Indian philosophical materials are traced as sources and intellectual influences in Emerson's American thought
interpretive_note: Important anti-linearity control: even after Raju/Prakash internal Indian-history cases and Embree/Nakamura comparative work, India also continues to function in a classic influence-on-West genealogy.

author: Warren E. Gates
title: The Spread of Ibn Khaldun's Ideas on Climate and Culture
role_description: Tracks possible spread/influence of Ibn Khaldun's climate/culture ideas toward later European thinkers
interpretive_note: Return of an influence/spread architecture; useful against Fakhry 1965 internal-object mode.

author: Carl T. Jackson
title: The Meeting of East and West: The Case of Paul Carus
role_description: Paul Carus as a site of intellectual encounter, mediation and attempted synthesis between Asian religious/philosophical materials and American thought
interpretive_note: Shows East-West mediation remaining a major JHI architecture after internally addressed Asian thought had already become possible; role regimes coexist rather than replace one another.

author: Hajime Nakamura
title: Review: Donald F. Lach, Asia in the Making of Europe
role_description: Asian specialist evaluates a major Europe-Asia transmission history inside JHI
interpretive_note: Important governance/network bridge: Nakamura later becomes Corresponding Editor, after Wiener-East-West collaboration.

author: Robert C. Williams
title: The Russian Soul: A Study in European Thought and Non-European Nationalism
role_description: A European nationalist vocabulary is appropriated and transformed in Russian self-definition and then circulates back into European social criticism
interpretive_note: Especially useful relation-role case: the article explicitly rejects a one-way borrowing model and treats transfer as cyclical; a phrase/category can be borrowed while the articulated idea becomes locally specific.

author: Jeffrey L. Klaiber
title: The Non-Communist Left in Latin America
role_description: Latin-American socialist/anti-imperialist thought treated as a regional intellectual-political formation with its own reformulations of imported left traditions
interpretive_note: Further evidence that autonomous Latin-American intellectual history is established in JHI before the 1975 explicit historiographical assessment of Zea.

author: Ronald Hilton
title: Is Intellectual History Irrelevant? The Case of the Aztecs
role_description: Review-article testing intellectual-history relevance where ancient/colonial past intersects contemporary ethnic-political appropriation
interpretive_note: Do not call this a decolonial-method manifesto without full text; current evidence supports a critique of romanticized/exaggerated Aztec heritage in contemporary identity politics.

author: Julia Ching
title: Truth and Ideology: The Confucian Way (Tao) and its Transmission (Tao-T'ung)
role_description: Two-millennia internal construction of Confucian orthodoxy, succession and ideological transmission
interpretive_note: Strong late-Wiener internal-object example: transmission now occurs within Chinese intellectual history, not chiefly China→West or West→China.

author: Jorge J. E. Gracia
title: Importance of the History of Ideas in Latin America: Zea's Positivism in Mexico
role_description: Latin-American history of ideas itself becomes the object of methodological/historiographical evaluation
interpretive_note: Institutional culmination of Wiener-Zea convergence: JHI now discusses the importance of an autonomous regional historia de las ideas tradition.
